Legal Envelope Sizes: Dimensions & Mailing Guide

Legal envelopes (#11, #12, #14) range from 4.5"×10.375" to 5"×11.5" and fit folded 8.5×14 legal-size paper. Get dimensions, postage, and which to use.

Legal envelopes are sized to fit legal-size 8.5 by 14 inch paper folded once. The most common is the #14 envelope at 5 by 11.5 inches (127 by 292.1 millimeters), which fits 8.5 by 14 paper folded in half lengthwise. The #11 (4.5 by 10.375 inches) and #12 (4.75 by 11 inches) are smaller variants for trifolded legal paper. All three qualify for First-Class letter postage starting at $0.78 in 2026.
Envelope Specifications
Dimensions (inches) 5" × 11.5" (#14, most common)
Dimensions (mm) 127mm × 292.1mm
Weight Limit 3.5
USPS Postage Class First-Class letter
Primary Uses
  • Mailing legal-size (8.5×14) documents folded
  • Law firm correspondence
  • Real estate closings and deeds
  • Long-format contracts
  • Court filings and legal notices

"Legal envelope" doesn't refer to a single standardized size. It refers to a category of long, narrow envelopes designed to hold legal-size 8.5 by 14 inch paper either folded in half or folded in thirds.

The three most common legal envelope sizes:

  • #14 envelope — 5 by 11.5 inches; fits 8.5 by 14 paper folded in half (the largest and most common)
  • #12 envelope — 4.75 by 11 inches; fits 8.5 by 14 paper folded in thirds
  • #11 envelope — 4.5 by 10.375 inches; fits 8.5 by 14 paper folded in thirds

All three sit at letter rate as long as they're flexible and under 0.25 inches thick. This page covers which size to use for which use case, postage rules, and how legal envelopes compare to the more common #10.

When to use a legal envelope

Mailing legal-size documents folded

Legal-size paper (8.5 by 14 inches) is still standard in law firms, real estate transactions, and certain government filings. When a document needs to mail folded but not trifolded — for example, a deed or contract that should remain readable with minimal handling — the #14 envelope at 5 by 11.5 inches is the right choice.

Law firm correspondence

Some firms use legal envelopes by tradition for outgoing correspondence, particularly for documents that pair with legal-size attachments. The #12 (4.75 × 11) is a common choice when the longer envelope is needed but the legal-paper insert is folded in thirds.

Real estate closings

Title companies and real estate attorneys mail closing documents in legal envelopes when the package includes deeds, settlement statements, or recorded documents on legal-size paper.

Court filings and legal notices

Courts that still accept paper filings often receive documents in legal envelopes addressed to the clerk of court. State and local government filings on legal paper similarly use these formats.

When to choose #10 instead

If your contents are 8.5 by 11 (letter-size) rather than 8.5 by 14 (legal-size), use a #10 envelope. The #10 is more readily stocked, costs less, and is recognized at every postal facility. Legal envelopes are specialized stock and may need to be specially ordered.

Legal envelope postage and USPS rules

All three common legal envelope sizes (#11, #12, #14) qualify for First-Class letter postage as long as they meet standard letter-rate requirements.

2026 First-Class postage for legal envelopes

  • 1 ounce, Forever stamp: $0.78
  • 1 ounce, metered postage: $0.74
  • Each additional ounce, up to 3.5 ounces: $0.29

Aspect ratio check

Legal envelopes are long and narrow, which puts them on the high end of the USPS aspect-ratio range:

  • #14 (5 × 11.5): aspect ratio 2.30 — within range
  • #12 (4.75 × 11): aspect ratio 2.32 — within range
  • #11 (4.5 × 10.375): aspect ratio 2.31 — within range

All three sit safely inside the machinable range of 1.3 to 2.5.

Common surcharge triggers

Legal envelope mailings often trigger surcharges for two reasons:

  • Multiple folded documents stacked together can exceed the 0.25 inch thickness limit
  • Multi-page filings often weigh more than 3.5 ounces, which moves the piece to flat rate

For legal mailings with substantial paperwork, a 9×12 flat envelope at flat rate is often more economical than overweight letter rate plus the surcharge — and the documents arrive unfolded.

Last verified: May 2026. Source: USPS Domestic Mail Manual 201.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the standard legal envelope size?

The most common legal envelope is the #14, measuring 5 by 11.5 inches (127 by 292.1 millimeters). It fits 8.5 by 14 inch legal-size paper folded in half lengthwise. Smaller variants include the #12 (4.75" × 11") and #11 (4.5" × 10.375").

What size envelope fits legal paper?

For 8.5 by 14 inch legal paper folded in half, use a #14 envelope (5 × 11.5). For legal paper folded in thirds, use a #12 (4.75 × 11) or #11 (4.5 × 10.375). For unfolded legal documents, use a 10×15 catalog envelope or larger.

Are legal envelopes letter rate or flat rate?

All three common legal envelope sizes (#11, #12, #14) qualify for First-Class letter postage at $0.78 in 2026, provided they are flexible, under 0.25 inches thick, and under 3.5 ounces.

What's the difference between a legal envelope and a #10?

A #10 envelope (4.125 × 9.5) fits 8.5 by 11 letter-size paper folded in thirds. Legal envelopes are longer (10.375 to 11.5 inches) and designed to fit 8.5 by 14 legal-size paper. Use #10 for letter-size correspondence; use legal envelopes for legal-size documents.

Where can I buy legal envelopes?

Legal envelopes are specialty stock — most office supply stores carry #14 envelopes, but #11 and #12 sizes are typically ordered through commercial printers or envelope specialists. Cornerstone stocks and prints all three sizes for client mailings.
